He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville Cardinals]]. ==Early life and high school== Brown grew up in [[Orlando, Florida]] and initially attended [[Orlando Christian Prep]]. After his sophomore year, he opted to leave Orlando Christian Prep to join the [[Overtime Elite]] league as a non-professional player to preserve his collegiate eligibility.{{cite web |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2023/09/06/varsity-weekly-transfer-fall-sports-news/ |title=Mikel Brown jumps to Overtime Elite, Oak Ridge adds IMG star |work=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |date=September web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/mikel-brown-focused-improvement-over-185030004.html|title=Mikel Brown focused on improvement over recruiting|first=Jason|last=Jordan|website=[[Yahoo Sports]]|date=April 20, 2024}} Brown transferred to [[DME Academy]] in [[Daytona Beach, Florida]] for his senior year.{{cite web|url=https://www.tuscaloosanews.com/story/sports/college/sec/2024/10/24/alabama-basketball-gaining-momentum-with-5-star-2025-recruit-report/75718549007/|title=Alabama basketball gaining momentum with 5-star 2025 recruit|work=[[The Tuscaloosa News]]|date=October 24, 2024|last=Smarr|first=Emilee}} He was selected to play in the [[2025 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] during his senior year.{{cite web|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/2025/01/27/mcdonalds-all-americans-basketball-mikel-brown-jr-louisville-malachi-moreno-kentucky/77975502007/|title=Louisville's Mikel Brown Jr., Kentucky's Malachi Moreno get McDonald's All-American honors|work=[[Courier Journal]]|date=January 27, 2025|access-date=January 31, 2025}} Brown was also named to the Team USA roster for the [[Nike Hoop Summit]].{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/high-school/florida/louisville-commit-mikel-brown-jr-selected-to-usa-men-s-nike-hoop-summit-team-01jhs2r40z7r|title=Louisville Commit Mikel Brown Jr. Selected to USA Men’s Nike Hoop Summit Team|first=Ross|last=Van De Griek|website=[[SI.com]]|date=January 16, 2025}} Brown was a consensus five-star recruit and one of the top players in the 2025 class, according to major recruiting services.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/high-school/florida/5-star-pg-mikel-brown-jr-talks-recruitment-player-comparison-01jfkc38tcky|title=5-star PG Mikel Brown Jr. Talks Recruitment, Player Comparison|first=Ross|last=Van De Griek|website=[[SI.com]]|date=December 20, 2024}} He committed to play [[college basketball]] at [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]] over offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] and [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]].{{cite |website=theacc.com |language=en}} and to the ACC All-Rookie team and earned two ACC Player and Rookie of the Week awards on November 17, 2025{{Cite web |date=2025-11-17 |title=Duke’s Boozer, UofL’s Brown Jr. Share ACC Men’s Basketball Weekly Honors |url=http://theacc.com/news/2025/11/17/dukes-boozer-uofls-brown-jr-share-acc-mens-basketball-weekly-honors.aspx |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=theacc.com |language=en}} and February 16, 2025.{{Cite web |date=2026-02-16 |title=Louisville’s Brown Jr. Sweeps ACC Men’s Basketball Weekly Honors |url=http://theacc.com/news/2026/2/16/louisvilles-brown-jr-sweeps-acc-mens-basketball-weekly-honors.aspx |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=theacc.com |language=en}} He scored 45 points in a 118–77 win{{Cite web |title=NC State vs. Louisville Box Score (Men), February 9, 2026 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/boxscores/2026-02-09-00-louisville.html |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=Sports-Reference.com |language=en}} over [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]] on February 9, 2026, which broke [[Cooper Flagg]]'s ACC freshman single-game scoring record{{Cite web |title=Brown Jr. Breaks ACC Freshman Scoring Record, Ties Program Record in 118-77 Rout of NC State |url=https://gocards.com/news/2026/2/9/mens-basketball-brown-jr-breaks-acc-freshman-scoring-record-ties-program-record-in-118-77-rout-of-nc-state |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=University of Louisville Athletic |language=en}} and also tied [[Wes Unseld]]'s scoring record at Louisville and set the school record with 10 three-pointers made. He scored at least 10 points in 16 of 21 outings with 20-plus points nine times,{{Cite web |title=Mikel Brown Jr. 2025-26 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/mikel-brown-jr-1/gamelog/2026 |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=Sports-Reference.com |language=en}} including three 29-point performances against [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (November 11, 2025{{Cite web |title=Kentucky vs. Louisville Box Score (Men), November 11, 2025 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/boxscores/2025-11-11-00-louisville.html |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}), [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] (February 14, 2026{{Cite web |title=Louisville vs. Baylor Box Score (Men), February 14, 2026 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/boxscores/2026-02-14-01-baylor.html |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}, added six assists and a career-high five steals) and [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]] (February 23, 2026{{Cite web |title=Louisville vs. Southern Methodist Box Score (Men), February 17, 2026 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/boxscores/2026-02-17-19-southern-methodist.html |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}). Brown opted out of the NCAA tournament due to a back injury.{{cite news |last=Crawford |first=Brad |title=Louisville star freshman Mikel Brown out for NCAA Tournament opener vs. South Florida |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/louisville-freshman-mikel-brown-out-ncaa-tournament-opener-south-florida/ |access-date=April 17, 2026 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=March 18, 2026}} He declared for the [[2026 NBA draft]] after the season.{{cite news |last=Spears |first=Marc |title=Louisville freshman Mikel Brown Jr. to declare for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/48420740 |access-date=April 17, 2026 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=April 7, 2026}} == Professional career == On June 23, 2026, Brown was selected with the sixth overall pick by the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in the [[2026 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-select-mikel-brown-jr-and-joshua-jefferson-in-2026-nba-draft|title=Brooklyn Nets Select Mikel Brown Jr. and Joshua Jefferson in 2026 NBA Draft|website=nba.com|date=June 24, 2026|access-date=July 11, 2026}} ==National team career== Brown has competed internationally for the United States in multiple occasions. He won gold with the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|2025 USA Men's U19 National Team]] at the [[2025 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2025 FIBA U19 Men's World Cup]] after averaging 14.9 points, 6.1 assists and 2.1 rebounds per game while shooting 47.6% from 3-point territory as the team went 7–0 in the tournament.{{Cite web |title=Mikel Brown Jr. |url=https://www.usab.com/players/mikel-brown-jr |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=USA Basketball |language=en}} He also played on the 2025 USA Men's [[Nike Hoop Summit]] Team that defeated the World Select Team, 124–114, in overtime.{{Cite web |title=USA Defeats World Team in Overtime of 2025 Men’s Nike Hoop Summit, 124-114 |url=https://www.usab.com/news/2025/04/usa-defeats-world-team-in-overtime-of-2025-mens-nike-hoop-summit-124-114 |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=USA Basketball |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=2025 Men's Nike Hoop Summit Box Score |url=https://www.usab.com/ |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=USA Basketball |language=en}} Brown scored 17 points while going 15 of 18 from the free throw line in that game, tying the most free throws ever made by a USA player in the event's history. He earned his first gold medal while playing on the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States under-18 basketball team]] at the [[2024 FIBA Under-18 AmeriCup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2025/01/13/louisville-basketball-recruiting-2025-class-pat-kelsey-mikel-brown-jr-ncaa/77432613007/|title=Louisville basketball signee Mikel Brown Jr. embracing chance to help Pat Kelsey rebuild|work=[[Courier Journal]]|date=January 13, 2025|access-date=January 31, 2025}} He started in all six games of that tournament and averaged 10.3 points, 3.3 rebounds and 4.8 assists to earn All-Star Five honors, leading the team in assists and minutes played. ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College===
